title: How to Use Conditional Formatting in Excel
dek: Conditional formatting changes a cell's color automatically based on its value — to highlight, rank, or flag data. Select your cells, open Home > Conditional Formatting, and pick a rule. Here is how to use every type, step by step.

seo.metaTitle: How to Use Conditional Formatting in Excel
seo.metaDescription: Use conditional formatting in Excel to color cells by value: highlight rules, top/bottom, data bars, color scales, and custom formulas. Step-by-step guide.

richText: Conditional formatting makes Excel color your cells automatically based on what they contain — turning a plain table into something you can read at a glance. Use it to highlight values above a target, flag overdue dates, rank the top performers, or spot duplicates. Once a rule is set, the colors update on their own as the data changes.

items: Select the cells you want to format.
Choose a rule type from the menu (see the types below).
Set the condition and pick a color or style, then click OK.

rows: Color cells greater than, less than, between, equal to, or containing text
Highlight the top 10, bottom 10, or above/below average
Draw a small bar in each cell, sized by its value
Shade cells on a gradient (for example, red-to-green)
Add arrows, traffic lights, or ratings based on value

body.text: A quick example: highlight values over a target

items: Select the sales figures in column B.
Home > Conditional Formatting > Highlight Cells Rules > Greater Than.
Type your target (say 1000) and choose a green fill. Click OK.

richText: Every value over 1000 turns green instantly, and any new number you type is colored automatically.

body.richText: To highlight duplicates, use Highlight Cells Rules > Duplicate Values. It is the fastest way to spot repeats before you clean them up.

To remove formatting: Conditional Formatting > Clear Rules, then choose selected cells or the whole sheet.
Rules are listed in priority order in Manage Rules — the top rule wins when two overlap.

items.question: How do I highlight an entire row with conditional formatting?
items.answerRichText: Use a formula rule. Select the whole range, choose New Rule > "Use a formula", and lock the column with a dollar sign — for example =$C2="Overdue". Because the column is fixed, Excel formats the full row whenever the test is true.

items.question: Why is my conditional formatting not working?
items.answerRichText: The usual causes are the wrong range selected, a formula missing the dollar sign, or a higher-priority rule overriding it. Open Conditional Formatting > Manage Rules to check the range, the formula, and the order of rules.

items.question: How do I copy conditional formatting to other cells?
items.answerRichText: Select a formatted cell, click Format Painter on the Home tab, then drag over the target cells. The rules copy across, adjusting their references to the new cells.
